renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: qc_pca_embedding
  title: Sample PCA from the pipeline QC
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample placed on the first two principal components that the pipeline computed on its count matrix, coloured by the matrix it came from. It answers whether the samples separate the way the experimental design predicts.
    How to read: replicates of one condition should sit together and different conditions apart. A sample far from its replicates, or a split that follows a batch instead of the condition, points to an outlier or a batch effect to resolve before reading any differential result.
    Source: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html
  kind: embedding
  config:
    axis_prefix: PC
  roles:
    sample_id: sample_id
    dim_1: dim_1
    dim_2: dim_2
    color: pca_set

- component: card
  title: Variance on the first component
  description: |-
    The hero number is the share of variance the first principal component explains, shown against 100 percent. It answers how much of the variation one axis carries.
    How to read: a large share means one dominant source of variation, ideally the condition. A small share means variation is spread over many axes and no single factor dominates.
  column: dim_1_percent
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - min
  - median
  secondary_layout: gauge
  coverage_max: 100.0
  caption: minimum and median, across contrasts

- component: table
  title: PCA coordinates
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its coordinates on the first two components and the share of variance each explains. It answers where a given sample sits and which count matrix it belongs to.
    How to read: sort by a component to find the outermost samples, then check them in the PCA tile.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: qc_distance_heatmap
  title: Sample distance heatmap
  description: |-
    Each cell is the Euclidean distance between two samples, computed on the variance-stabilised expression the pipeline QC used, and the rows and columns are clustered. It answers which samples resemble each other.
    How to read: replicates should form dark blocks of small distance and conditions should separate. A sample that clusters with the wrong group, or sits far from everything, is an outlier to inspect.
    Note: the diagonal is zero by construction.
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: sample

- component: table
  title: Sample distance table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its distance to every other sample. It answers the exact value behind a cell of the heatmap.
    How to read: sort a column to find the samples nearest or furthest from one sample.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: volcano
  title: Differential expression volcano
  description: |-
    Each point is a gene in one contrast: its log2 fold change on the horizontal axis and its adjusted p-value on the vertical axis. It answers which genes change most, in which direction, and how confidently.
    How to read: genes in the upper left and upper right corners are strongly down- and up-regulated with high confidence. A cloud with almost nothing past the lines means little differential signal, so check the QQ view and the sample PCA before trusting the contrast. Open the table tile to inspect the labelled genes.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is the adjusted p-value cut-off of 0.05 and the vertical lines mark an absolute log2 fold change of 1 (a fold change of 2). Both are the nf-core/differentialabundance defaults, which also define the up, down and not significant calls on every tile of this tab.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  kind: volcano
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.05
    effect_threshold: 1.0
    top_n_labels: 10
    effect_label: Log2 fold change
    significance_label: -log10 adjusted p-value
  roles:
    feature_id: gene_id
    effect_size: log2fc
    significance: padj
    category: contrast

- component: advanced_viz
  id: ma
  title: Fold change against mean expression
  description: |-
    Each point is a gene in one contrast: its mean normalised expression on the horizontal axis (log2 of base mean plus one) and its log2 fold change on the vertical axis. It answers whether the fold changes are real or only come from weakly expressed genes.
    How to read: a healthy MA plot is a flat cloud centred on zero, with the significant genes spread across expression levels. A funnel that widens at low expression is normal noise of low counts. A cloud shifted away from zero points to a normalisation problem, so check the sample distributions.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal lines mark an absolute log2 fold change of 1 (a fold change of 2) and points are highlighted when the adjusted p-value is below 0.05. Both are the nf-core/differentialabundance defaults. DESeq2 itself colours its MA plot at an adjusted p-value of 0.1, its default alpha.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json and https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html
  kind: ma
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.05
    fold_change_threshold: 1.0
    top_n_labels: 10
    effect_label: Log2 fold change
    intensity_label: Mean expression (log2)
  roles:
    feature_id: gene_id
    avg_log_intensity: log2_base_mean
    log2_fold_change: log2fc
    significance: padj

- component: advanced_viz
  id: qq
  title: P-value QQ plot
  description: |-
    Each point is a gene: its observed raw p-value, as minus log10, against the value expected if no gene differed between the groups. One trace is drawn per contrast. It answers whether the test statistics are well calibrated.
    How to read: points hugging the diagonal for most of the range and lifting off at the far end mean a few real signals over a calibrated null. A curve that leaves the diagonal early, or sits below it, points to inflation or deflation from batch effects, a wrong design or low counts. Compare the contrasts and revisit the PCA when one curve differs.
    Lines and annotations: the diagonal is y = x, the expectation when p-values are uniformly distributed under no effect. The shaded band is the 95% confidence interval of that null, so points inside it are consistent with chance.
  kind: qq
  config:
    show_ci: true
    show_identity: true
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    p_value: pvalue
    category: contrast
    feature_id: gene_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: da_barplot
  title: Top changed genes per contrast
  description: |-
    Each bar is a gene: its log2 fold change in a contrast, for the genes with the largest absolute change. It answers which genes drive each contrast and in which direction.
    How to read: long bars to the right are up-regulated and to the left down-regulated; bars are marked when their adjusted p-value passes the cut-off. A strong fold change without significance usually means low or variable counts, so open the MA plot and the table to check it.
    Lines and annotations: significance is marked at an adjusted p-value below 0.05, the nf-core/differentialabundance default.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  kind: da_barplot
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.05
    effect_label: Log2 fold change
  roles:
    feature_id: gene_id
    contrast: contrast
    lfc: log2fc
    significance: padj

- component: card
  title: Fold change spread
  description: |-
    The hero number is the range of log2 fold changes over every gene and contrast in view, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how large the differences are overall.
    How to read: a box tight around zero with a long range means most genes are unchanged and a few change a lot. A box shifted off zero points to a normalisation issue. Filter to one contrast to compare them.
  column: log2fc
  aggregation: range
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: quartiles of the fold changes

- component: card
  title: Significant genes by direction
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct genes called significant, and the bars rank them by direction, up or down. It answers whether the response is mostly induction or repression.
    How to read: a strong imbalance between up and down is worth checking against the normalisation, the sample PCA and the biology. Calls use an adjusted p-value below 0.05 and an absolute log2 fold change of at least 1.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  column: gene_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: direction
  top_n_count: 3
  filter_expr: col('direction') != 'not significant'
  caption: significant genes, by direction

- component: card
  title: Calls by direction
  description: |-
    Each unit is one gene in one contrast, and the ring splits them into up, down and not significant. It answers how many genes pass the cut-offs overall.
    How to read: a ring that is mostly not significant means a weak contrast or too little replication. Open the volcano to see the borderline genes.
    Lines and annotations: the call is an adjusted p-value below 0.05 and an absolute log2 fold change of at least 1, the nf-core/differentialabundance defaults.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  column: direction
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - mode
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: direction
  caption: calls, by direction; most frequent call
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Strength of the strongest call
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest minus log10 adjusted p-value, and the histogram shows the distribution of that score over all genes. It answers how strong the best evidence is and how much of the table carries any evidence.
    How to read: a histogram piled at zero with a long right tail is the usual shape. DESeq2 reports an adjusted p-value of exactly 0 for its strongest calls, which the score caps at 300, so the maximum is a ceiling and not a measurement.
  column: neg_log10_padj
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - q3
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: distribution, with its median and upper quartile

- component: figure
  title: Distribution of fold changes
  description: |-
    Each bar counts genes in a log2 fold change bin, split by call. It answers how the significant genes sit in the overall fold change distribution.
    How to read: a distribution centred on zero with significant genes in both tails is expected. A skewed or shifted distribution suggests a composition effect or a normalisation problem. Open the MA plot to confirm.
    Lines and annotations: the call colours use an adjusted p-value below 0.05 and an absolute log2 fold change of at least 1, the nf-core/differentialabundance defaults. The dashed line is the median log2 fold change of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of DESeq2.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: log2fc
    color: direction
    labels:
      log2fc: Log2 fold change
      direction: Call
  reference_lines:
  - axis: x
    stat: median
    column: log2fc

- component: table
  title: Differential results table
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene in one contrast with its DESeq2 statistics: base mean, log2 fold change, standard error, p-value, adjusted p-value and the call. It answers which genes to follow up and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by adjusted p-value or by fold change, and filter by call. A missing adjusted p-value means DESeq2 filtered the gene as an outlier or as too low in counts.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: gene_id

- component: card
  title: Call composition
  description: |-
    Each unit is one gene in one contrast and the bar shows the share of each call. It answers what fraction of the tested genes change.
    How to read: compare the shares with the ring above; a very small significant share means few genes pass an adjusted p-value of 0.05 and a log2 fold change of 1.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  column: direction
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: direction
  caption: calls, as shares; number of call classes

- component: card
  title: Median adjusted p-value
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median adjusted p-value over all genes and contrasts, compared with a cut-off. It answers whether most of the table carries evidence of change.
    How to read: a median below the cut-off means most genes are significant, which is unusual outside a strong perturbation. A median near one is the normal case.
    Lines and annotations: the cut-off is an adjusted p-value of 0.05, the nf-core/differentialabundance default, and the warning level is 0.1, the default alpha of DESeq2 results().
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json and https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html
  column: padj
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 0.05
  threshold_direction: max
  threshold_warn: 0.1
  caption: median, with its smallest and largest

- component: advanced_viz
  id: manhattan
  title: Significance along the genome
  description: |-
    Each point is a gene placed at its start coordinate, with minus log10 of its adjusted p-value on the vertical axis. It answers where on the genome the differentially expressed genes cluster.
    How to read: isolated tall points are single genes, while a tower of points over one region suggests a shared locus effect such as a copy number change or a cluster of related genes. Colour by direction to see whether a region moves one way. Several contrasts overlap here, so filter to one.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is an adjusted p-value of 0.05, shown as 1.301 on the minus log10 axis. It is the nf-core/differentialabundance default cut-off. The score is capped at 300 where DESeq2 reports an adjusted p-value of 0.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  kind: manhattan
  config:
    score_threshold: 1.301
    score_kind: -log10 adjusted p-value
    color_by_columns:
    - direction
    - gene_biotype
    default_color_by: direction
    top_n_labels: 8
  roles:
    chr: chromosome
    pos: start
    score: neg_log10_padj
    feature: gene_name
    effect: log2fc

- component: advanced_viz
  id: annotated_volcano
  title: Volcano with gene symbols
  description: |-
    Each point is a gene in one contrast, labelled by its symbol: log2 fold change on the horizontal axis and adjusted p-value on the vertical axis. It answers which named genes change most and how confidently.
    How to read: genes in the upper left and upper right corners are strongly down- and up-regulated with high confidence. Few points past the lines means little differential signal. Open the table tile to inspect the labelled genes.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is the adjusted p-value cut-off of 0.05 and the vertical lines mark an absolute log2 fold change of 1 (a fold change of 2). Both are the nf-core/differentialabundance defaults.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  kind: volcano
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.05
    effect_threshold: 1.0
    top_n_labels: 10
    effect_label: Log2 fold change
    significance_label: -log10 adjusted p-value
  roles:
    feature_id: gene_name
    effect_size: log2fc
    significance: padj
    category: contrast

- component: advanced_viz
  id: annotated_da_barplot
  title: Top changed genes with symbols
  description: |-
    Each bar is a gene, named by its symbol, with its log2 fold change in a contrast, for the genes with the largest absolute change. It answers which named genes drive each contrast and in which direction.
    How to read: long bars to the right are up-regulated and to the left down-regulated; bars are marked when their adjusted p-value passes the cut-off. A strong fold change without significance usually means low counts, so check the volcano and the table.
    Lines and annotations: significance is marked at an adjusted p-value below 0.05, the nf-core/differentialabundance default.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  kind: da_barplot
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.05
    effect_label: Log2 fold change
  roles:
    feature_id: gene_name
    contrast: contrast
    lfc: log2fc
    significance: padj

- component: advanced_viz
  id: chromosome_lollipop
  title: Calls along each chromosome
  description: |-
    Each lollipop is a gene placed at its start coordinate on its chromosome, sized by the size of its log2 fold change and coloured by call (up, down or not significant). It answers how the differential calls spread along each chromosome.
    How to read: a run of same-coloured lollipops close together suggests a regional effect, such as a copy number gain or a gene cluster. Calls spread evenly with no pattern are the usual case. Open the Manhattan view to see the same genes by significance.
    Lines and annotations: the calls are an adjusted p-value below 0.05 and an absolute log2 fold change of at least 1, the nf-core/differentialabundance defaults. The labels name the most extreme genes.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  kind: lollipop
  config:
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    feature_id: chromosome
    position: start
    category: direction
    effect: log2fc
    label: gene_name

- component: card
  title: Genes by biotype
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct annotated genes, and the bars rank the biotypes that hold most of them. It answers what kind of genes the table covers.
    How to read: protein coding genes dominate most annotations. A table rich in non-coding biotypes points to a different assay or to an annotation that includes them.
  column: gene_name
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: gene_biotype
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: genes, by biotype

- component: card
  title: Chromosome coverage
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of chromosomes with at least one gene, and the bar splits the rows by chromosome. It answers whether the table spans the genome or only part of it.
    How to read: a bar dominated by one chromosome means the table was restricted or a region is over-represented.
  column: chromosome
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: chromosome
  caption: rows, by chromosome

- component: card
  title: Fold change spread
  description: |-
    The hero number is the range of log2 fold changes over every gene in view, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how large the differences are.
    How to read: a box tight around zero with a long range means most genes are unchanged and a few change a lot. A box shifted off zero points to a normalisation issue.
  column: log2fc
  aggregation: range
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: quartiles of the fold changes

- component: figure
  title: Calls by gene biotype
  description: |-
    Each bar counts genes of one biotype, split by call (up, down or not significant). It answers which kinds of genes respond.
    How to read: compare the coloured share of each biotype. A biotype with a larger share of up or down calls than its neighbours is enriched for change.
    Lines and annotations: the calls are an adjusted p-value below 0.05 and an absolute log2 fold change of at least 1, the nf-core/differentialabundance defaults.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: gene_biotype
    color: direction
    labels:
      gene_biotype: Gene biotype
      direction: Call

- component: table
  title: Annotated results table
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene in one contrast with its DESeq2 statistics and its symbol, chromosome, coordinates and biotype. It answers which genes to follow up and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by adjusted p-value or fold change, and filter by chromosome or biotype to focus on a region or gene class.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: gene_id

- component: card
  title: Biotype concentration
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct biotypes, and the bar shows how concentrated the rows are in the top ones. It answers whether one gene class dominates the table.
    How to read: a high concentration is normal for protein coding genes. A flat split means a mixed annotation.
  column: gene_biotype
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: concentration
  breakdown_col: gene_biotype
  caption: rows, by biotype share

- component: card
  title: Calls by direction
  description: |-
    Each unit is one gene in one contrast, and the ring splits them into up, down and not significant. It answers how many genes pass the cut-offs.
    How to read: a ring that is mostly not significant means a weak contrast. Open the volcano to see the borderline genes.
    Lines and annotations: the call is an adjusted p-value below 0.05 and an absolute log2 fold change of at least 1, the nf-core/differentialabundance defaults.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  column: gene_name
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: direction
  caption: calls, by direction

- component: card
  title: Expression level by biotype
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median base mean, the average normalised count, over all genes, and the bars rank biotypes by their median. It answers how strongly the genes are expressed and which classes are highest.
    How to read: low medians mean the data is shallow and the fold changes are noisy, so lean on adjusted p-values. Base mean spans orders of magnitude, which is why it is ranked and not drawn as a box.
  column: base_mean
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - q1
  - q3
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: gene_biotype
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: median, with its quartiles, by biotype

- component: card
  title: Significance distribution
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median minus log10 adjusted p-value over all genes, and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how much of the table carries any evidence.
    How to read: a pile at zero with a long right tail is the usual shape. DESeq2 reports an adjusted p-value of exactly 0 for its strongest calls, which the score caps at 300.
  column: neg_log10_padj
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - q3
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: distribution, with its upper quartile and maximum

- component: card
  title: Chromosomes with most genes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of chromosomes, and the bars rank the ones with the most rows. It answers where the tested genes sit.
    How to read: large chromosomes lead in an unrestricted table. An unexpected leader points to a regional effect or a filtered table.
  column: chromosome
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: chromosome
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: genes, by chromosome

- component: card
  title: Significance spread
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median minus log10 adjusted p-value, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how the evidence is spread across genes.
    How to read: a median near zero with a thin upper box is the normal case. A high median means a strong perturbation.
  column: neg_log10_padj
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Smallest adjusted p-value
  description: |-
    The hero number is the smallest adjusted p-value in view, compared with a cut-off. It answers whether any gene reaches significance.
    How to read: a value above the cut-off means nothing is called; check replication and the design before tuning thresholds.
    Lines and annotations: the cut-off is an adjusted p-value of 0.05, the nf-core/differentialabundance default, and the warning level is 0.1, the default alpha of DESeq2 results().
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json and https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html
  column: padj
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 0.05
  threshold_direction: max
  threshold_warn: 0.1
  caption: smallest, with its median

- component: advanced_viz
  id: distance_matrix
  title: Sample distances
  description: |-
    Each cell is the Euclidean distance between two samples over the most variable features of the variance-stabilised matrix, with rows and columns clustered. It answers which samples are most alike overall.
    How to read: replicates should form blocks of small distance and conditions should separate. A sample that joins the wrong block, or sits far from all others, is an outlier or a mislabelled library.
    Source: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: distribution_profile
  title: Expression density per sample
  description: |-
    Each curve is one sample: the share of its expressed features in each bin of variance-stabilised expression, on a grid shared by every sample. It answers whether the libraries have the same shape before any comparison is made.
    How to read: curves should overlay each other. A curve shifted along the axis, or with a shorter upper tail, is normalised differently from its neighbours and every contrast inherits that. Features at the matrix floor are left out of the curves and reported as a share on the card.
    Source: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Variance-stabilised expression (log2 scale)
    y_title: Share of expressed features
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: sample_id
    x: bin_centre
    y: density

- component: card
  title: Median expression across samples
  description: |-
    The hero number is the range of sample medians of variance-stabilised expression, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how far apart the libraries sit.
    How to read: a narrow range means comparable libraries. One sample far from the rest is a candidate outlier; find it on the density tile.
  column: median
  aggregation: range
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: quartiles of the sample medians

- component: card
  title: Share of features at the floor
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average share of features sitting at the floor of the matrix, the value given to genes with no counts, and the histogram shows the spread over samples. It answers how many genes are effectively unexpressed.
    How to read: similar shares across samples are expected. A sample with a much larger share is shallower or lower in complexity than its neighbours.
  column: floor_share
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: distribution, with its median and maximum

- component: card
  title: Samples per group
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of samples, and the bars rank the groups of the sample sheet by their number of samples. It answers how balanced the design is.
    How to read: very uneven groups make contrasts less reliable, and a group with one sample cannot be tested.
  column: sample_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: group
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: samples, by group

- component: table
  title: Expression summary per sample
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample and expression bin, with the sample's group and its five-number summary of variance-stabilised expression. It answers the exact numbers behind each curve.
    How to read: filter to one sample to read its quartiles and its share at the floor.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: top_variable_heatmap
  title: Most variable features
  description: |-
    Each cell is the variance-stabilised expression of one of the most variable genes (rows) in one sample (columns), with the sample sheet factors as column annotations. It answers which genes drive the differences between samples.
    How to read: columns of the same condition should share a pattern. A column that looks like the other group, or a block of genes that follows a batch factor, shows what structures the data before any contrast is run.
    Source: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: gene_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: pca
  title: Sample PCA
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample placed on the first principal components of the variance-stabilised expression of its most variable genes, coloured by group. It answers whether the samples separate by the factor under study.
    How to read: replicates of one group should sit together and groups apart. A sample away from its group, or a split along a batch factor, is an outlier or a confounder to deal with before differential testing. Switch the colour to a batch column to check it.
    Source: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html
  kind: embedding
  config:
    axis_prefix: PC
  roles:
    sample_id: sample_id
    dim_1: dim_1
    dim_2: dim_2
    color: group

- component: card
  title: Samples per group
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of samples, and the bars rank the groups by their number of samples. It answers how balanced the design is.
    How to read: very uneven groups make contrasts less reliable, and a group with one sample cannot be tested.
  column: sample_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: group
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: samples, by group

- component: card
  title: Spread on the first component
  description: |-
    The hero number is the range of sample scores on the first principal component, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how widely samples spread on the leading axis.
    How to read: a wide range with a clear gap suggests two clusters, usually the groups. Check the PCA tile to see which samples sit at each end.
  column: dim_1
  aggregation: range
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: quartiles of the sample scores

- component: table
  title: PCA coordinates and sample sheet
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its principal component scores and the factors of the sample sheet. It answers which factors line up with the components.
    How to read: sort by a component and look for a factor that follows it.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: qc_pca_embedding
  title: Sample PCA from the pipeline QC
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample placed on the first two principal components that the pipeline computed on its count matrix, coloured by the matrix it came from. It answers whether the samples separate the way the experimental design predicts.
    How to read: replicates of one condition should sit together and different conditions apart. A sample far from its replicates, or a split that follows a batch instead of the condition, points to an outlier or a batch effect to resolve before reading any differential result.
    Source: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html
  kind: embedding
  config:
    axis_prefix: PC
  roles:
    sample_id: sample_id
    dim_1: dim_1
    dim_2: dim_2
    color: pca_set

- component: card
  title: Variance on the first component
  description: |-
    The hero number is the share of variance the first principal component explains, shown against 100 percent. It answers how much of the variation one axis carries.
    How to read: a large share means one dominant source of variation, ideally the condition. A small share means variation is spread over many axes and no single factor dominates.
  column: dim_1_percent
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - min
  - median
  secondary_layout: gauge
  coverage_max: 100.0
  caption: minimum and median, across contrasts

- component: table
  title: PCA coordinates
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its coordinates on the first two components and the share of variance each explains. It answers where a given sample sits and which count matrix it belongs to.
    How to read: sort by a component to find the outermost samples, then check them in the PCA tile.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: qc_distance_heatmap
  title: Sample distance heatmap
  description: |-
    Each cell is the Euclidean distance between two samples, computed on the variance-stabilised expression the pipeline QC used, and the rows and columns are clustered. It answers which samples resemble each other.
    How to read: replicates should form dark blocks of small distance and conditions should separate. A sample that clusters with the wrong group, or sits far from everything, is an outlier to inspect.
    Note: the diagonal is zero by construction.
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: sample

- component: table
  title: Sample distance table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its distance to every other sample. It answers the exact value behind a cell of the heatmap.
    How to read: sort a column to find the samples nearest or furthest from one sample.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: volcano
  title: Differential expression volcano
  description: |-
    Each point is a gene in one contrast: its log2 fold change on the horizontal axis and its adjusted p-value on the vertical axis. It answers which genes change most, in which direction, and how confidently.
    How to read: genes in the upper left and upper right corners are strongly down- and up-regulated with high confidence. A cloud with almost nothing past the lines means little differential signal, so check the QQ view and the sample PCA before trusting the contrast. Open the table tile to inspect the labelled genes.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is the adjusted p-value cut-off of 0.05 and the vertical lines mark an absolute log2 fold change of 1 (a fold change of 2). Both are the nf-core/differentialabundance defaults, which also define the up, down and not significant calls on every tile of this tab.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  kind: volcano
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.05
    effect_threshold: 1.0
    top_n_labels: 10
    effect_label: Log2 fold change
    significance_label: -log10 adjusted p-value
  roles:
    feature_id: gene_id
    effect_size: log2fc
    significance: padj
    category: contrast

- component: advanced_viz
  id: ma
  title: Fold change against mean expression
  description: |-
    Each point is a gene in one contrast: its mean normalised expression on the horizontal axis (log2 of base mean plus one) and its log2 fold change on the vertical axis. It answers whether the fold changes are real or only come from weakly expressed genes.
    How to read: a healthy MA plot is a flat cloud centred on zero, with the significant genes spread across expression levels. A funnel that widens at low expression is normal noise of low counts. A cloud shifted away from zero points to a normalisation problem, so check the sample distributions.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal lines mark an absolute log2 fold change of 1 (a fold change of 2) and points are highlighted when the adjusted p-value is below 0.05. Both are the nf-core/differentialabundance defaults. DESeq2 itself colours its MA plot at an adjusted p-value of 0.1, its default alpha.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json and https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html
  kind: ma
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.05
    fold_change_threshold: 1.0
    top_n_labels: 10
    effect_label: Log2 fold change
    intensity_label: Mean expression (log2)
  roles:
    feature_id: gene_id
    avg_log_intensity: log2_base_mean
    log2_fold_change: log2fc
    significance: padj

- component: advanced_viz
  id: qq
  title: P-value QQ plot
  description: |-
    Each point is a gene: its observed raw p-value, as minus log10, against the value expected if no gene differed between the groups. One trace is drawn per contrast. It answers whether the test statistics are well calibrated.
    How to read: points hugging the diagonal for most of the range and lifting off at the far end mean a few real signals over a calibrated null. A curve that leaves the diagonal early, or sits below it, points to inflation or deflation from batch effects, a wrong design or low counts. Compare the contrasts and revisit the PCA when one curve differs.
    Lines and annotations: the diagonal is y = x, the expectation when p-values are uniformly distributed under no effect. The shaded band is the 95% confidence interval of that null, so points inside it are consistent with chance.
  kind: qq
  config:
    show_ci: true
    show_identity: true
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    p_value: pvalue
    category: contrast
    feature_id: gene_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: da_barplot
  title: Top changed genes per contrast
  description: |-
    Each bar is a gene: its log2 fold change in a contrast, for the genes with the largest absolute change. It answers which genes drive each contrast and in which direction.
    How to read: long bars to the right are up-regulated and to the left down-regulated; bars are marked when their adjusted p-value passes the cut-off. A strong fold change without significance usually means low or variable counts, so open the MA plot and the table to check it.
    Lines and annotations: significance is marked at an adjusted p-value below 0.05, the nf-core/differentialabundance default.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  kind: da_barplot
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.05
    effect_label: Log2 fold change
  roles:
    feature_id: gene_id
    contrast: contrast
    lfc: log2fc
    significance: padj

- component: card
  title: Fold change spread
  description: |-
    The hero number is the range of log2 fold changes over every gene and contrast in view, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how large the differences are overall.
    How to read: a box tight around zero with a long range means most genes are unchanged and a few change a lot. A box shifted off zero points to a normalisation issue. Filter to one contrast to compare them.
  column: log2fc
  aggregation: range
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: quartiles of the fold changes

- component: card
  title: Significant genes by direction
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct genes called significant, and the bars rank them by direction, up or down. It answers whether the response is mostly induction or repression.
    How to read: a strong imbalance between up and down is worth checking against the normalisation, the sample PCA and the biology. Calls use an adjusted p-value below 0.05 and an absolute log2 fold change of at least 1.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  column: gene_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: direction
  top_n_count: 3
  filter_expr: col('direction') != 'not significant'
  caption: significant genes, by direction

- component: card
  title: Calls by direction
  description: |-
    Each unit is one gene in one contrast, and the ring splits them into up, down and not significant. It answers how many genes pass the cut-offs overall.
    How to read: a ring that is mostly not significant means a weak contrast or too little replication. Open the volcano to see the borderline genes.
    Lines and annotations: the call is an adjusted p-value below 0.05 and an absolute log2 fold change of at least 1, the nf-core/differentialabundance defaults.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  column: direction
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - mode
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: direction
  caption: calls, by direction; most frequent call
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Strength of the strongest call
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest minus log10 adjusted p-value, and the histogram shows the distribution of that score over all genes. It answers how strong the best evidence is and how much of the table carries any evidence.
    How to read: a histogram piled at zero with a long right tail is the usual shape. DESeq2 reports an adjusted p-value of exactly 0 for its strongest calls, which the score caps at 300, so the maximum is a ceiling and not a measurement.
  column: neg_log10_padj
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - q3
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: distribution, with its median and upper quartile

- component: figure
  title: Distribution of fold changes
  description: |-
    Each bar counts genes in a log2 fold change bin, split by call. It answers how the significant genes sit in the overall fold change distribution.
    How to read: a distribution centred on zero with significant genes in both tails is expected. A skewed or shifted distribution suggests a composition effect or a normalisation problem. Open the MA plot to confirm.
    Lines and annotations: the call colours use an adjusted p-value below 0.05 and an absolute log2 fold change of at least 1, the nf-core/differentialabundance defaults. The dashed line is the median log2 fold change of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of DESeq2.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: log2fc
    color: direction
    labels:
      log2fc: Log2 fold change
      direction: Call
  reference_lines:
  - axis: x
    stat: median
    column: log2fc

- component: table
  title: Differential results table
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene in one contrast with its DESeq2 statistics: base mean, log2 fold change, standard error, p-value, adjusted p-value and the call. It answers which genes to follow up and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by adjusted p-value or by fold change, and filter by call. A missing adjusted p-value means DESeq2 filtered the gene as an outlier or as too low in counts.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: gene_id

- component: card
  title: Call composition
  description: |-
    Each unit is one gene in one contrast and the bar shows the share of each call. It answers what fraction of the tested genes change.
    How to read: compare the shares with the ring above; a very small significant share means few genes pass an adjusted p-value of 0.05 and a log2 fold change of 1.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  column: direction
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: direction
  caption: calls, as shares; number of call classes

- component: card
  title: Median adjusted p-value
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median adjusted p-value over all genes and contrasts, compared with a cut-off. It answers whether most of the table carries evidence of change.
    How to read: a median below the cut-off means most genes are significant, which is unusual outside a strong perturbation. A median near one is the normal case.
    Lines and annotations: the cut-off is an adjusted p-value of 0.05, the nf-core/differentialabundance default, and the warning level is 0.1, the default alpha of DESeq2 results().
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json and https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html
  column: padj
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 0.05
  threshold_direction: max
  threshold_warn: 0.1
  caption: median, with its smallest and largest

- component: advanced_viz
  id: manhattan
  title: Significance along the genome
  description: |-
    Each point is a gene placed at its start coordinate, with minus log10 of its adjusted p-value on the vertical axis. It answers where on the genome the differentially expressed genes cluster.
    How to read: isolated tall points are single genes, while a tower of points over one region suggests a shared locus effect such as a copy number change or a cluster of related genes. Colour by direction to see whether a region moves one way. Several contrasts overlap here, so filter to one.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is an adjusted p-value of 0.05, shown as 1.301 on the minus log10 axis. It is the nf-core/differentialabundance default cut-off. The score is capped at 300 where DESeq2 reports an adjusted p-value of 0.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  kind: manhattan
  config:
    score_threshold: 1.301
    score_kind: -log10 adjusted p-value
    color_by_columns:
    - direction
    - gene_biotype
    default_color_by: direction
    top_n_labels: 8
  roles:
    chr: chromosome
    pos: start
    score: neg_log10_padj
    feature: gene_name
    effect: log2fc

- component: advanced_viz
  id: annotated_volcano
  title: Volcano with gene symbols
  description: |-
    Each point is a gene in one contrast, labelled by its symbol: log2 fold change on the horizontal axis and adjusted p-value on the vertical axis. It answers which named genes change most and how confidently.
    How to read: genes in the upper left and upper right corners are strongly down- and up-regulated with high confidence. Few points past the lines means little differential signal. Open the table tile to inspect the labelled genes.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is the adjusted p-value cut-off of 0.05 and the vertical lines mark an absolute log2 fold change of 1 (a fold change of 2). Both are the nf-core/differentialabundance defaults.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  kind: volcano
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.05
    effect_threshold: 1.0
    top_n_labels: 10
    effect_label: Log2 fold change
    significance_label: -log10 adjusted p-value
  roles:
    feature_id: gene_name
    effect_size: log2fc
    significance: padj
    category: contrast

- component: advanced_viz
  id: annotated_da_barplot
  title: Top changed genes with symbols
  description: |-
    Each bar is a gene, named by its symbol, with its log2 fold change in a contrast, for the genes with the largest absolute change. It answers which named genes drive each contrast and in which direction.
    How to read: long bars to the right are up-regulated and to the left down-regulated; bars are marked when their adjusted p-value passes the cut-off. A strong fold change without significance usually means low counts, so check the volcano and the table.
    Lines and annotations: significance is marked at an adjusted p-value below 0.05, the nf-core/differentialabundance default.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  kind: da_barplot
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.05
    effect_label: Log2 fold change
  roles:
    feature_id: gene_name
    contrast: contrast
    lfc: log2fc
    significance: padj

- component: advanced_viz
  id: chromosome_lollipop
  title: Calls along each chromosome
  description: |-
    Each lollipop is a gene placed at its start coordinate on its chromosome, sized by the size of its log2 fold change and coloured by call (up, down or not significant). It answers how the differential calls spread along each chromosome.
    How to read: a run of same-coloured lollipops close together suggests a regional effect, such as a copy number gain or a gene cluster. Calls spread evenly with no pattern are the usual case. Open the Manhattan view to see the same genes by significance.
    Lines and annotations: the calls are an adjusted p-value below 0.05 and an absolute log2 fold change of at least 1, the nf-core/differentialabundance defaults. The labels name the most extreme genes.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  kind: lollipop
  config:
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    feature_id: chromosome
    position: start
    category: direction
    effect: log2fc
    label: gene_name

- component: card
  title: Genes by biotype
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct annotated genes, and the bars rank the biotypes that hold most of them. It answers what kind of genes the table covers.
    How to read: protein coding genes dominate most annotations. A table rich in non-coding biotypes points to a different assay or to an annotation that includes them.
  column: gene_name
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: gene_biotype
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: genes, by biotype

- component: card
  title: Chromosome coverage
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of chromosomes with at least one gene, and the bar splits the rows by chromosome. It answers whether the table spans the genome or only part of it.
    How to read: a bar dominated by one chromosome means the table was restricted or a region is over-represented.
  column: chromosome
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: chromosome
  caption: rows, by chromosome

- component: card
  title: Fold change spread
  description: |-
    The hero number is the range of log2 fold changes over every gene in view, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how large the differences are.
    How to read: a box tight around zero with a long range means most genes are unchanged and a few change a lot. A box shifted off zero points to a normalisation issue.
  column: log2fc
  aggregation: range
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: quartiles of the fold changes

- component: figure
  title: Calls by gene biotype
  description: |-
    Each bar counts genes of one biotype, split by call (up, down or not significant). It answers which kinds of genes respond.
    How to read: compare the coloured share of each biotype. A biotype with a larger share of up or down calls than its neighbours is enriched for change.
    Lines and annotations: the calls are an adjusted p-value below 0.05 and an absolute log2 fold change of at least 1, the nf-core/differentialabundance defaults.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: gene_biotype
    color: direction
    labels:
      gene_biotype: Gene biotype
      direction: Call

- component: table
  title: Annotated results table
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene in one contrast with its DESeq2 statistics and its symbol, chromosome, coordinates and biotype. It answers which genes to follow up and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by adjusted p-value or fold change, and filter by chromosome or biotype to focus on a region or gene class.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: gene_id

- component: card
  title: Biotype concentration
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct biotypes, and the bar shows how concentrated the rows are in the top ones. It answers whether one gene class dominates the table.
    How to read: a high concentration is normal for protein coding genes. A flat split means a mixed annotation.
  column: gene_biotype
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: concentration
  breakdown_col: gene_biotype
  caption: rows, by biotype share

- component: card
  title: Calls by direction
  description: |-
    Each unit is one gene in one contrast, and the ring splits them into up, down and not significant. It answers how many genes pass the cut-offs.
    How to read: a ring that is mostly not significant means a weak contrast. Open the volcano to see the borderline genes.
    Lines and annotations: the call is an adjusted p-value below 0.05 and an absolute log2 fold change of at least 1, the nf-core/differentialabundance defaults.
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json
  column: gene_name
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: direction
  caption: calls, by direction

- component: card
  title: Expression level by biotype
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median base mean, the average normalised count, over all genes, and the bars rank biotypes by their median. It answers how strongly the genes are expressed and which classes are highest.
    How to read: low medians mean the data is shallow and the fold changes are noisy, so lean on adjusted p-values. Base mean spans orders of magnitude, which is why it is ranked and not drawn as a box.
  column: base_mean
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - q1
  - q3
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: gene_biotype
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: median, with its quartiles, by biotype

- component: card
  title: Significance distribution
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median minus log10 adjusted p-value over all genes, and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how much of the table carries any evidence.
    How to read: a pile at zero with a long right tail is the usual shape. DESeq2 reports an adjusted p-value of exactly 0 for its strongest calls, which the score caps at 300.
  column: neg_log10_padj
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - q3
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: distribution, with its upper quartile and maximum

- component: card
  title: Chromosomes with most genes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of chromosomes, and the bars rank the ones with the most rows. It answers where the tested genes sit.
    How to read: large chromosomes lead in an unrestricted table. An unexpected leader points to a regional effect or a filtered table.
  column: chromosome
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: chromosome
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: genes, by chromosome

- component: card
  title: Significance spread
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median minus log10 adjusted p-value, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how the evidence is spread across genes.
    How to read: a median near zero with a thin upper box is the normal case. A high median means a strong perturbation.
  column: neg_log10_padj
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Smallest adjusted p-value
  description: |-
    The hero number is the smallest adjusted p-value in view, compared with a cut-off. It answers whether any gene reaches significance.
    How to read: a value above the cut-off means nothing is called; check replication and the design before tuning thresholds.
    Lines and annotations: the cut-off is an adjusted p-value of 0.05, the nf-core/differentialabundance default, and the warning level is 0.1, the default alpha of DESeq2 results().
    Source: https://github.com/nf-core/differentialabundance/blob/master/nextflow_schema.json and https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html
  column: padj
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 0.05
  threshold_direction: max
  threshold_warn: 0.1
  caption: smallest, with its median

- component: advanced_viz
  id: distance_matrix
  title: Sample distances
  description: |-
    Each cell is the Euclidean distance between two samples over the most variable features of the variance-stabilised matrix, with rows and columns clustered. It answers which samples are most alike overall.
    How to read: replicates should form blocks of small distance and conditions should separate. A sample that joins the wrong block, or sits far from all others, is an outlier or a mislabelled library.
    Source: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: distribution_profile
  title: Expression density per sample
  description: |-
    Each curve is one sample: the share of its expressed features in each bin of variance-stabilised expression, on a grid shared by every sample. It answers whether the libraries have the same shape before any comparison is made.
    How to read: curves should overlay each other. A curve shifted along the axis, or with a shorter upper tail, is normalised differently from its neighbours and every contrast inherits that. Features at the matrix floor are left out of the curves and reported as a share on the card.
    Source: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Variance-stabilised expression (log2 scale)
    y_title: Share of expressed features
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: sample_id
    x: bin_centre
    y: density

- component: card
  title: Median expression across samples
  description: |-
    The hero number is the range of sample medians of variance-stabilised expression, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how far apart the libraries sit.
    How to read: a narrow range means comparable libraries. One sample far from the rest is a candidate outlier; find it on the density tile.
  column: median
  aggregation: range
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: quartiles of the sample medians

- component: card
  title: Share of features at the floor
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average share of features sitting at the floor of the matrix, the value given to genes with no counts, and the histogram shows the spread over samples. It answers how many genes are effectively unexpressed.
    How to read: similar shares across samples are expected. A sample with a much larger share is shallower or lower in complexity than its neighbours.
  column: floor_share
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: distribution, with its median and maximum

- component: card
  title: Samples per group
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of samples, and the bars rank the groups of the sample sheet by their number of samples. It answers how balanced the design is.
    How to read: very uneven groups make contrasts less reliable, and a group with one sample cannot be tested.
  column: sample_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: group
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: samples, by group

- component: table
  title: Expression summary per sample
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample and expression bin, with the sample's group and its five-number summary of variance-stabilised expression. It answers the exact numbers behind each curve.
    How to read: filter to one sample to read its quartiles and its share at the floor.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: top_variable_heatmap
  title: Most variable features
  description: |-
    Each cell is the variance-stabilised expression of one of the most variable genes (rows) in one sample (columns), with the sample sheet factors as column annotations. It answers which genes drive the differences between samples.
    How to read: columns of the same condition should share a pattern. A column that looks like the other group, or a block of genes that follows a batch factor, shows what structures the data before any contrast is run.
    Source: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: gene_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: pca
  title: Sample PCA
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample placed on the first principal components of the variance-stabilised expression of its most variable genes, coloured by group. It answers whether the samples separate by the factor under study.
    How to read: replicates of one group should sit together and groups apart. A sample away from its group, or a split along a batch factor, is an outlier or a confounder to deal with before differential testing. Switch the colour to a batch column to check it.
    Source: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html
  kind: embedding
  config:
    axis_prefix: PC
  roles:
    sample_id: sample_id
    dim_1: dim_1
    dim_2: dim_2
    color: group

- component: card
  title: Samples per group
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of samples, and the bars rank the groups by their number of samples. It answers how balanced the design is.
    How to read: very uneven groups make contrasts less reliable, and a group with one sample cannot be tested.
  column: sample_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: group
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: samples, by group

- component: card
  title: Spread on the first component
  description: |-
    The hero number is the range of sample scores on the first principal component, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how widely samples spread on the leading axis.
    How to read: a wide range with a clear gap suggests two clusters, usually the groups. Check the PCA tile to see which samples sit at each end.
  column: dim_1
  aggregation: range
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: quartiles of the sample scores

- component: table
  title: PCA coordinates and sample sheet
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its principal component scores and the factors of the sample sheet. It answers which factors line up with the components.
    How to read: sort by a component and look for a factor that follows it.
